en: The Apadāna of the Elder Cūḷasugandha Bhaddiya Chapter 10 I was once a merchant’s son, named Sugandha, in the city of Bhaddiya. I was well-versed in the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas, and I was skilled in all branches of knowledge. At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, the Teacher of the World, appeared in the world. Having renounced the household life for the homeless state, he attained supreme enlightenment. He traveled from village to village, from town to town, and eventually arrived at Bhaddiya. There, the Blessed One stayed in the Jātiyā Grove, surrounded by a great assembly of monks. Hearing that the Buddha had arrived, I went to the presence of the Blessed One. Having approached him, I paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. As I sat there, the Blessed One taught me the Dhamma, which is excellent in the beginning, excellent in the middle, and excellent in the end; he explained the holy life in its full detail, both in spirit and in letter. Having heard the Dhamma, my mind was filled with joy. Then, having taken up faith, I went forth from the household life into homelessness under the Blessed One. Having gone forth, I applied myself with diligence and energy. In no long time, I realized the goal of the holy life for which sons of noble family rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness. I directly knew: "Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being. I became one of the arahants. This was my first aspiration: "May I become an arahant like the Blessed One. By virtue of that root of merit, I have now attained the fruit of arahantship. Thus, through the power of that wholesome deed, I have reached the final Nibbāna. This is the account of the Elder Cūḷasugandha, the tenth in the Bhaddiya Chapter.
“In this auspicious aeon,
there was one of great renown, a kinsman of Brahmā,
Kassapa by lineage.”
The best among those who speak arose.
Endowed with the secondary marks and possessing the thirty-two excellent primary characteristics;
Enveloped by a fathom-wide radiance,
overspread with a network of rays,
he was like the moon that brings comfort.
Like the sun, he is the maker of light;
like a cloud, he is the extinguisher [of suffering];
like the ocean, he is a mine of virtues.
Like the earth in virtue,
like the Himalayas in concentration,
and like space in wisdom.
Unattached like the wind.
At that time, I was reborn in Bārāṇasī into a great family;
Amidst abundant wealth and grain,
a collection of various jewels,
and with a great retinue—
Approaching the Leader of the World as he sat there, I listened to the Dhamma,
which was as enchanting as the Deathless.
Bearing the thirty-two marks,
like the moon together with its constellations,
he was endowed with the secondary characteristics.
Like a blossoming king of Sāla trees,
surrounded by a network of rays,
he shines like the golden mountain Meru.
Surrounded by a fathom-wide radiance,
like the sun with its hundred rays,
the Supreme Victor has a face of gold.
Like a mountain peak, he was like a monk;
with a heart full of compassion,
he was like the ocean in virtue.
The Hero, whose fame is renowned throughout the world, who is like Sineru, the best of mountains,
and who is spread wide with glory.
The Sage is like space;
his mind is unattached everywhere,
and the Leader is like the wind.
The support for all beings,
like the earth, is the Seventh Sage;
he is unsullied by the world.
Like a lotus in water,
you shine like a mass of fire, burning away the thicket of false doctrines.
Like a panacea that destroys the poison of all defilements everywhere,
like Mount Gandhamādana,
Adorned with the fragrance of virtues,
the hero is a mine of virtues,
like the ocean is of jewels.
Like a victorious great warrior,
he is the remover of the stains of defilement from the rows of forest trees along the Indus.
The crusher of Māra’s army,
that king is like a wheel-turning monarch,
possessing the jewels of the factors of enlightenment.
Resembling a great physician,
a healer of the disease of hatred,
like a surgeon who is a doctor.
He was the one who split open the tumor of false views.
At that time, he was the lamp of the world,
honored by humans, gods, and Sakka.
The Conqueror, a sun among men, teaches the Dhamma to the assemblies:
"Having given a gift, one becomes possessed of great wealth."
"By virtue one reaches the state of a Sugata;
by cultivation one attains Nibbāna"—
thus you should instruct them.
All the assemblies listen to that teaching, which is greatly delightful and beautiful in its beginning, middle, and end.
Like the great taste of the Deathless,
having heard the most sweet Dhamma,
he was filled with confidence in the Conqueror’s teaching.
Having gone for refuge to the Sugata,
may I pay homage to the Sage’s Perfumed Chamber for as long as life lasts.
Then I sprinkled the earth with four kinds of fragrant scents for eight days during that month.
Having made a resolution for the fragrance of his body,
which was then emitting a foul odor,
the Conqueror then gave this prophecy:
Having attained a fragrant body:
"Whoever once scatters fragrance upon the ground of the Perfume Chamber;
By the ripening of that karma,
he was reborn here and there with a fragrant body everywhere.
This man shall become one endowed with the fragrance of virtues, and having extinguished the taints,
he will attain Nibbāna.
By that well-performed kamma,
and by my intentions and aspirations,
having abandoned this human body,
I went to the realm of the Thirty-three.
And now, in my final existence,
I have been born into a brahmin family.
While I was dwelling in the womb,
my mother was made fragrant by my body; and when [I emerged] from my mother’s womb,
Then I departed from the city;
you blew as if perfumed with all the fragrances of Sāvatthī.
And a fragrant rain of flowers,
divine in scent and delightful,
as well as highly precious incenses—
At that time,
the devas perfumed that house with all kinds of fragrances, incense, and flowers.
They perfumed with fragrance the house in which I was born;
and when I was young and auspicious,
Standing in the prime of youth,
the Charioteer of Men then disciplined Sela and his assembly.
Surrounded by all of them,
he arrived at the city of Sāvatthī;
then, that majesty of the Buddha—
Having seen this, I went forth.
[I have realized] virtue, concentration, wisdom,
and unsurpassed liberation.
Having developed these four qualities,
I attained the destruction of the taints.
When I had gone forth, I...
And when I was an Arhat,
and when I was about to attain Parinibbāna,
there was a rain of fragrances at that time.
The fragrance of my body always surpasses the most precious sandalwood, campaka, and lotus;
likewise, it excels all other perfumes in every respect.
Having overcome them, I strive here and there;
my defilements have been incinerated...
[etc.]
I dwell free from taints.
Welcome indeed has come to me... [as before] ...
This is the teaching of the Buddha.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
“Such is the teaching of the Buddha.
Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Cūḷasugandha spoke these verses.
This is the tenth legend of the Elder Cūḷasugandha.
The Fifty-fifth Chapter: The Bhaddiya Group.
Its summary verse:
Bhaddiya, Revata, and the Elder...
And Sīvalī was one who gains great profit;
so too were Vaṅgīsa, Nandaka,
Kāḷudāyī, and Abhaya.
Lomaso, Vanavaccho,
and Sugandho as the tenth;
there are three hundred verses therein.
And sixteen more than that.
Now, the summary of the chapters:
the chapter called Kaṇikāra.
Phalada and Tiṇadāyaka;
Kaccāna and Bhaddiya;
this is the group, and these verses have been counted.
Herein, there are nine hundred and eighty-four verses,
plus five hundred and fifty.
The Apadānas have been revealed;
together with the Udāna verses,
they amount to six thousand.
And two hundred and eighteen verses.
